subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw make the DeepSeek prefix-cache workaround a public model compatibility option with a DeepSeek default, or keep the policy internal and config-free?
rationale: Both approaches can address the regression, but only maintainers can accept the permanent plugin/config contract and upgrade-time provider behavior; code review and live proof cannot choose that product boundary.

options.title: Adopt DeepSeek compat option
options.body: Rebase and land this DeepSeek-only, explicitly overridable strategy with its existing live provider proof and regression coverage.

options.title: Prefer config-free policy
options.body: Use the competing internal strategy only after it has equivalent current-head live DeepSeek proof and a clear provider scope that avoids broad proxy regressions.

options.title: Pause both implementations
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open until provider owners define a different cache-policy seam or upstream behavior changes.

recommendation.title: Adopt DeepSeek compat option
recommendation.body: Rebase and land this DeepSeek-only, explicitly overridable strategy with its existing live provider proof and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to DeepSeek/provider compatibility and the exported compatibility surface requiring the product decision.
